newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: P&G aims to double global sales in 10 years.
newsitem.headline: P&G aims to double global sales in 10 years.

text.p: Procter & Gamble (P&G) will boost efficiency and investments in an effort to double its global revenue of $35 billion during the next decade, said John Pepper, the consumer products company's chairman and chief executive.
"Our goals going ahead are aggressive," he said at a reception with business executives in Argentina on Wednesday night. "We aim to double the size of our business in the next 10 years."
Pepper said two key factors for the company's growth were technical innovation and globalization.
"Before World War II we were almost entirely a U.S. company. Today, more than half of our $35 billion revenue comes from outside the United States, and we are doing business in 140 countries."
The company is celebrating its 160th anniversary this year, which makes it the second oldest of the biggest 50 U.S. industrial companies, Pepper said.
P&G produces or sells more than 300 trademark products, including disposable diapers, feminine care and hair care products, detergents and potato snacks.
Pepper said one of Procter & Gamble's key strategies for expanding business was to identify the fastest developing countries "like China, Brazil, Chile and Argentina."

He praised the Mercosur customs union -- comprised of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay -- saying it allowed the company to export products from Argentina to Brazil and to import raw materials from Brazil to Argentina at an advantage.
Singling out Argentina, he said the company aimed to double its $300 million annual revenue generated in that country in less than five years.
Since 1990 the company has invested $250 million in the country, where it has four plants and a head office, and its local workforce grew to 1,600 from 45, he said.

Pepper said the average age of Argentine consumers was 27 years, compared with 34 in the United States. "This is very important as we consider the consumer develops its consuming habits through all his life," he said.
"Argentina is particularly important as the middle class in this country is larger than in any other southern cone country by far," he said.
Pepper said the company wanted to enhance its relations with suppliers and customers, and to develop contacts with universities to recruit young people.
He told Reuters that P&G was "planning new, very significant investments, particularly in Brazil and Argentina", but he declined to elaborate.

"We aim to improve quality. Innovation is moving faster than ever in all the categories we are in: disposable diapers, feminine protection, hair care, laundry, all of which we are making here except for hair care."

"So we will be upgrading our plants, bringing in new equipment to handle new material to improve efficiency. Most of it (the investment) would be in that area, and I would expect it over the next four years. The other major investments certainly will be in marketing."
